title: GS21 product economy (gvyp10) with a SECOND nonlinear loading, a curvature in productivity on the priced shock x: a larger factor model
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is the PRODUCT of two within-firm states that two different characteristics reveal, so the premium is bilinear in the ranks?
notes:
GROUP 4 (larger factor models) in GS21, which had no such cell. gvyp10 (exposure = productivity x coupon on the priced state y) plus a second nonlinear loading on the already-priced productivity shock x: the x loading becomes gs_bx + gs_bx2 (z~^2 - 1)/sqrt(2) with gs_bx2 1.0, a curvature in productivity that is a distinct cross-sectional pattern from the y loading's product. No second chain is needed. The reduced-form latent ladder (finding 21) says room and gap rise with the number of interaction-loaded factors; this is its structural test at K = 2.

PRE-CHECK (low resolution, 2026-10-12, gsshape.py): ranks R2 0.51 / pairwise products 0.94 / market 49% / cs-sd of the premium 4.9 %/yr, against gvyp10's 0.48 / 0.90 / 51% / 4.6: the second loading adds a little nonlinear dispersion. gs_bx2 0.3 and 0.6 are between.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; id read from the Quest solve log before any seed runs. Mechanism probe.

PREDICTION (2026-10-12, before the run): room above gvyp10's +0.194 and a fair gap at or above +0.0196; FALSIFIED as 'a second interaction factor adds' if the fair gap is below gvyp10's on the same seeds in 7 of 10.

changes: gs_bv [0.1] x gs_bzb 1.0 z~ b~: productivity x coupon exposure, single type
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv gs_bzb z~ b~ y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
